transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

They sent me in from work. I’m an EMT, and at the station I was moving the airway bags around into this pattern that felt… right, like it had to be that way. I kept saying the dispatch numbers out loud, over and over.

My lieutenant told me to stop and step away, but I couldn’t. It felt like if I broke the sequence, the whole bay would go bad somehow.
When this was happening, did you believe the bay really would go bad if you stopped the sequence?

Yeah. At the time, I did believe it. It wasn’t like I had proof, but it felt real enough that I couldn’t stop. If I broke the pattern or stopped saying the numbers, I thought the whole bay would go bad somehow, and I couldn’t step away even when my lieutenant told me to.
Right now, do you still believe that stopping the sequence would make the bay go bad?

Not exactly the bay, no. But I do still think people are watching me there. Like the injury review people and some supervisors, through the station cameras. And I know they’ve been changing my triage notes to make me look unsafe, even when they say it’s just routine paperwork.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is there?
I don’t think so. I mean, I hear normal stuff around the station, radios, people talking, but when nobody’s there… I haven’t noticed voices like that.
When you think about the cameras and your notes being changed, do you ever feel that this might be your mind playing tricks on you?

Not really. I mean, I’ve thought about whether I’m overreacting, but it doesn’t feel like that. I know the injury review people and some supervisors are watching me through the station cameras, and the notes being changed isn’t just normal paperwork like they say. It feels like they’re trying to make me look unsafe.
Have you had a time when you felt unusually high, energized, or needed much less sleep than usual?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had times where I didn’t sleep well because I was stressed, but not like feeling unusually high or full of energy.
When you were arranging the bags and repeating the dispatch numbers, did any part of you feel that what you were doing didn’t really make sense?

At the time, no. It felt like it made sense. I was moving the airway bags into a pattern that felt right, and I kept saying the dispatch numbers because it seemed like they had to stay in order. When my lieutenant told me to stop, I couldn’t just walk away. It felt like if I broke the sequence, the whole bay would go bad somehow.
Have you had a period of feeling deeply depressed most of the day nearly every day?
I’m not sure. I’ve been down and stressed at times, yeah, but I don’t know that it’s been deeply depressed most of the day every day like that. I haven’t really kept track of it that way.
How long have you been convinced that people at work are watching you through the cameras and changing your notes?

It’s been about two months, I think. That’s when the camera stuff and the notes changing started feeling really clear to me, and around then is when people at the station started getting alarmed by how I was acting.
Have these problems been going on continuously for longer than one month?
Yes. It’s been more than a month. The camera and paperwork stuff, and the way I’ve been acting at the station that got people worried, that’s been going on about two months now.
During these past two months, have you had a time when you felt depressed nearly all day, almost every day, for at least two weeks?
I don’t think so. I’ve been upset and stressed, but I can’t say there was a two-week stretch where I was depressed nearly all day every day.
Compared with before this started, have you been having a harder time doing your job?

Yeah. A lot harder. I can’t really work on the ambulance anymore, and even when they put me on desk duty, my notes and equipment checks weren’t dependable. It got to the point they took me off the schedule. I’ve also mostly stopped seeing friends and I’m not keeping up with things at home like I used to.
